to complete, useful work.

TokenJunkieLabs requests USD 38,000 equivalent in XLM for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The work installs a useful paid Stellar service with two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators and the same selected operation through two independently operated facilitators.

The product is open-source, self-hostable merchant and buyer tooling. It carries an approved API request, dataset or paid MCP tool through native settlement, complete useful output, fulfillment and operating handover. The merchant controls its source and terms. The buyer controls its keys, request and spending. Another engineer can reopen the installation and recover unfinished work.

The working development baseline comprises 18 distinct team-operated purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM, with network fees recorded separately. The funded milestones establish independent customer operation, repeated use and production receiving from that baseline.

Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software for a merchant to sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and for its buyer to receive the complete result in an existing application. A purchase connects the approved request, native transfer, usable output and merchant fulfillment. That connection survives interrupted delivery, a changed source edition and handover to another maintainer.

We request $38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from award acceptance. The funded outcome is two independently operated merchant services and two independent buyer operators: installed services by day 30, recurring testnet use by day 90, and both merchants operating maintainable mainnet services by day 150. T2 runs the same useful service through two independently operated testnet facilitators.

The working product supplies the architecture and completed development foundation. The award funds the remaining source and receiving adaptations, Stellar deployment, monitoring and recovery improvements needed by the selected independent services. Those reusable improvements return to the public product.

Customer problem, need and adoption

Our first customer is a recurring API/data-service operator or the agency implementing that service in a customer's application. The commissioning payer buys installation and handover; the independent buyer pays for the useful resource. These roles may belong to different organizations.

For an analyst, completion requires the entire agreed population, original units and time basis, and a usable report. An agent application needs its approved result within the aggregate task budget. A paid page, signed transfer or finished background job is one part of that customer task. The merchant needs to connect accepted output to its offer, fulfillment and accounting.

Two supported installation patterns make the adoption plan concrete:

Installation patternUseful recurring purchaseCustomer acceptance
A merchant publishes a reviewed economic or operational report.The buyer acquires the agreed new reporting period or source edition and compares it with the prior result.Complete report and underlying selected data open in the customer's application, preserving units, periods and source meaning.
A merchant sells a typed dataset or saved query.The buyer acquires a distinct approved query or refreshed population, receiving every agreed paid page and file.The complete result reopens with its original request, source selection, aggregate cost and merchant records.

The selection fixes the source, geography or other population, observation period, query and expected customer output before purchase. The merchant reviews the release; the buyer receives the agreed HTML, CSV, JSON or named query result in its analyst workspace. The priced unit is exactly the advertised resource. If a complete task needs several paid pages or separately priced files, the workorder and buyer approval account for their combined cost and full coverage. A new source period or distinct useful query supplies the next purchase.

Veridex invited our existing buyer CLI into its testnet cohort and reported no third-party testing budget. Our latest reply proposes a paid buyer-integration pilot, partner funding or a specifically valued reciprocal workshare with agreed deliverables and usage rights. Blockscout expressed interest and reported no integration budget; Nansen declined. The detailed customer and commercial plan carries the corresponding installation roles and workshare scope.

For each selected installation, the workorder names the payer, merchant, buyer, receiving engineer, authorized source, complete task and output, priced unit, spending limit, host and acceptance owner. The first installed execution establishes the operating baseline. Each following agreed source period, edition or distinct query supplies useful repeat work. The receiving engineer performs an actual change or recovery before handover. That same recurring task continues through the T2 and T3 measurement windows.

A Timescale installation, if selected, applies this scope to original commissioning reports and native source populations, reviewed field/time/quality meanings, baseline-to-observed reconciliation and complete analytical receiving. An aid-data installation connects the original organisation publication and selected activity portfolios to the reviewed financial result, with original document links, captured evidence, named source review and complete analyst receiving. Their complete existing chapters supply the source and receiving architecture; the selected customer workorder determines the actual remaining adaptation and commercial responsibilities.

The purchase target follows the two selected buyers’ work. Two buyers making one purchase on each ordinary weekday generate twenty purchases in fourteen consecutive days. Their selected T3 workorders must establish actual demand for at least thirty distinct useful paid requests across those same two buyers and both merchants within the fourteen-day window. The additional demand comes from selected new source periods, useful queries or the complete advertised files and pages needed for their tasks. Each workorder defines the paid unit before purchase and retains its association with the complete customer task: two paid pages may finish one task, while the task total remains one. Reopening a saved result, retrying its original request and cached use preserve that original purchase and task. Work from another buyer can be evaluated in its own cohort.

The shipped Customer-use Calendar turns that agreement into a saved, dated operating plan within the original Installation. It retains the selected buyers, complete tasks, source periods and separate purchase or prepaid funding groups. Allowance use, reopening and free use remain distinct. An operator compares the saved schedule with the original cohort target, associates actual purchase records when available, and retains every later edit as a new Installation edition.

TokenJunkieLabs earns defined implementation fees and separately scoped care. Merchants retain resource receipts; implementation partners retain customer relationships. We measure adaptation effort, support workload, active customer effort, manual corrections and time to accepted output to establish the actual value and cost of each deployment.

Connected Systems commissioning. A prepared GeoRobotix workshare applies the product to one civil or environmental observation source: select the systems, datastreams, time window and returned JSON schema; retain complete acquisition coverage and original units; review a mapping; then deliver saved editions, queries, comparisons and an independently received operator workspace. The proposed implementation is $9,600 / 72 engineering hours / 12 active business days, with $4,800 at commencement and $4,800 at acceptance. First contact is prepared and unsent; no customer agreement or collection is recorded. The reusable native workflow has completed source review, query/export, separate receiving and cold reopen on the publisher’s illustrative observation. Customer installation, a live collection and its selected paid Stellar service remain future work. Original workshare · Maintained product and receiving guide.

Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar provides native authorization and settlement for the reviewed purchase. In its x402 Exact flow, the buyer signs a Soroban token-transfer authorization binding payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. A facilitator submits it on the selected network; fee sponsorship can cover the transaction fee. Our implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

The application retains the endpoint and method or MCP tool and arguments, request identity, selected source, payment option, complete output and fulfillment history. It checks the approved operation before dispatch and joins those application records to the original native transaction. Wallet authority and aggregate spending remain with the buyer; source, pricing and fulfillment authority remain with the merchant.

Stellar's own x402 CLI guide already covers the challenge, signed retry, returned response and transfer confirmation, and explains why saving the full returned body matters when another request incurs another payment. x402 facilitators supply verification and settlement; Bazaar supplies discoverable resource schemas. We reuse those foundations and carry the purchased resource through the complete customer task, its aggregate approval, unfinished-result recovery and merchant/accounting handover.

Existing products already provide substantial paid-access capabilities:

Published foundationOur funded application contribution
ApiCharge deploys typed endpoints and retains purchased route quality of service across pricing changes.Complete acquired data and reports continue in the customer's editable application and another engineer's installation.
MPP Router provides Stellar paid-service discovery, signed asynchronous-job polling and request-ID response caching.A recurring task retains its exact source/query, all agreed pages and files, original payment, customer output and maintainer recovery.

Our proposed Open Track contribution is that reusable merchant-to-customer workflow: typed source and receiving interfaces, complete purchase state across independent providers, deployed response and maintainable handover. The six packages implement these capabilities in two independent installations and publish the resulting improvements. Native payments, returning buyers and useful tasks another engineer can continue measure their value to Stellar. The architecture and ecosystem comparison develops the existing-tool comparison.

Defined architecture and operating behavior

Six connected components carry the customer task:

  1. Merchant workspace. A private operator selects an authorized source edition or named query, schema, output and limits. Source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
  2. HTTP or MCP resource. Source adapters preserve types, nulls, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential references govern source access.
  3. Buyer approval and budget. The buyer approves the exact method or tool, arguments, source scope and payment option. The original challenge and remote schema must match before signing; per-payment limits and the existing budget reservation govern aggregate spending.
  4. Stellar settlement. The native signer and facilitator use the reviewed network, asset, recipient, amount, expiry and fee policy. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the resulting transfer. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery lifecycle.
  5. Complete delivery and accounting. The application retains all agreed pages/files, original attempts, accepted output, merchant notification and acknowledgment. A prepaid request keeps its selected pass and consumed allowance when defaults change. Customer pricing retains quantity, period, tariff and supplier-cost basis beside its invoice or service records.
  6. Recovery and receiving. Confirmation, transfer, output and fulfillment keep separate states. An uncertain response is reconciled through its original dispatch. Another engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the original work.

Catalog-to-request continuity. The buyer service retains each complete original catalog page; the desk and typed clients carry its selected row and payment alternative through review. Browse and search continuations retain the operator's filters and the provider's coverage information. Declared HTTP path and query fields, or MCP tool arguments, guide explicit input. A path template becomes a concrete URL under the configured merchant route; fixed advertised values stay fixed. The native HTTP workflow then retains that exact request, body and spending limit in its original durable intent. Operators select the same service workspace when they reopen its status, recovery and saved output. Complete response downloads verify the retained byte count and hash. These capabilities are delivered in the buyer discovery and native request package.

Close recurring service. A merchant connects each prepaid service order to its customer, retains usage captures, and chooses the opening and closing records for the period. The customer workbench carries those records through reviewed statements, saved closing cycles, corrections and complete customer handovers. Purchase amounts, service activity and separately issued invoices remain available in their own financial records.

Node.js implements the browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces; source and receiving applications also use Python/SQLite and PHP/WordPress/WooCommerce. The defined scope builds on existing Stellar SDKs and contracts. Each deployed facilitator has explicit network, asset, recipient, signing-account and fee policies. T2 configures the same service for two compatible testnet operators; T3 deploys each merchant's reviewed mainnet configuration. The native signer and facilitator guide describes that operating foundation.

Working product and demonstrated results

Installation and recurring buyer work. The maintained product workflow connects a customer’s complete capability basket to an immutable source recipe, actual dependency manifests and its original native build. Command finder and the product catalogue expose the available commands and applications. A saved plan keeps the purpose, review and source inspection together after restart; its selected installation supplies the original Runtime handoff and a readable briefing with observed package versions. In Request Collections, original provider listings, selected payment alternatives and existing buyer operators become reusable request plans and named periods. The operator reviews those retained inputs and continues the original collection through approval, payment and complete receiving. This is the starting product for the selected services’ funded adaptation and independent handover.

Merchant cash and accountant continuity. The bank application connects original OFX/QFX/CSV statements to the merchant’s existing receipts, invoices and refunds. Both bank screens retain the same payment and source coverage, including gross receipts with separate fees, reviewed source corrections and customer remittance allocations. The operator reviews actual statement balances and retains a complete account close with original files, exact postings, customer exports and correction history. The installed operating handover carries this same accounting workspace through saved Applications and continued customer work.

Customer service closing and handover. The customer workbench connects customer profiles and order assignments to native usage captures. Operators plan service periods for several customers, inspect statement previews, issue or resume a saved closing cycle, and correct or withdraw a statement with linked history. Complete plans, saved cycles and grouped customer packets reopen with their statement files and status snapshots. The installed application, typed client and MCP interface share the same workflow.

Buyer discovery and native requests. The merged product now includes schema-aware catalog search, complete browse/search continuation, explicit request forms, typed buyer clients, a registry of existing native service workspaces, and the packaged mcp-catalog-journey command. The native HTTP path continues from the retained listing to preparation, operator-approved execution, history, recovery and the complete saved response. The source includes the concrete path-input workflow needed by the two published /inspect/:address resources. These are completed development foundations for the two selected merchant installations.

Functional discovery result, October 12, 2026. We captured the complete published Vellar testnet catalog: 27 HTTP GET resources in one 45,753-byte page, with the returned total matching the captured rows. We executed the actual dependency-free ranking and index functions in V8 against those same bytes. The comparison used 24 queries derived from the resources' published parameter names and descriptions, plus the nine retained baseline queries. Seventeen declaration-derived queries map to one original resource and seven map to two, giving 31 query-resource pairs. The nine general baseline probes have no declared expected-resource mapping and are included in the overall 33-query behavior comparison.

Declared parameter-to-resource relationships, 31 totalPrior rankingSchema-aware ranking
Source resource found in the returned results2231
Source resource present in the first three results1929

Eleven source-resource positions improved; the remaining positions were unchanged. Direct and indexed results matched for all 33 queries. For example, topic found both published quote resources in positions one and two, mode found both Base64 resources, and original found the diff resource in first position. This measures how well the published declarations lead a buyer to their own resources. The maintained replay package retains the comparison method for subsequent source editions. The captured catalog JSON and complete functional comparison accompany this application.

Threat response and outcome measurement

The T2 response package includes a documented threat model, its corresponding installed monitoring plan, and material corrections. Each installation records its source edition, authority, network, facilitator, protected records, observations, thresholds, notification destinations and primary/backup responders. Threats include changed offers or approvals, wrong payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted delivery, missing observations and restoration of the wrong generation. Each threat is linked to an observable signal, a monitor, an accountable responder and the recovery action; source and delivery failures receive the appropriate application-level observation. The plan follows Stellar's threat-modeling guidance and builder monitoring template.

The customer operates an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure, retaining financial and delivery states, notification and acknowledgment, response/recovery times and useful output. The receiving engineer reopens the original incident after restart; observation gaps remain visible.

A completed purchase requires one distinct approved intent, independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Transactions are deduplicated per network, with assets and fees recorded separately. A prepaid pass counts once after its first agreed operation produces complete accepted output; later calls are usage. A customer task completes when every agreed page, file and required order action is accepted. Thus the HPD acquisition is two purchases and one complete task.

T2 requires 10 purchases in total across two independent buyers during seven consecutive days ending by day 90. T3 requires 30 in total during fourteen consecutive days ending by day 150, with both buyers returning on another UTC day for a distinct completed purchase. Both merchants receive independent use. Independence refers to the accountable organization/person across agents and wallets.

Each cohort retains attempted, completed, partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. The original first attempt determines window membership; settlement and complete accepted output must occur within that window. Later observations retain their actual timing. The two-facilitator comparison uses the same service, schema, population and output.

Customer benefit compares the prior task, first installed execution and recurring use on the same population or period: active effort, manual corrections, time to accepted output and unresolved work. For a stated period, calculate direct labor value from completed tasks, comparable active hours saved and the customer's stated hourly value; subtract implementation and incremental provider, hosting, payment and support costs. The original workorder retains those inputs alongside accepted milestones, fees, collections and support effort.

Installed responsibility and response

The installation workorder records the responsible operator at each boundary. These responsibilities travel with the maintained service when its receiving engineer changes.

BoundaryResponsible operator and working handover
Source, offer and fulfillmentThe merchant selects the authorized source, publication and terms. Its operator retains the release history, full delivery result and original fulfillment/accounting case.

Delivery capacity, payment timing and sustainability

Bryce allocates contributors and operating resources to the six packages. The retained 400-hour/150-day resource model's lowest examined timely allocation is 25 engineering hours plus eight integration/handover hours per week. Capacity effect of a selected Connected Systems commission. The original GeoRobotix proposal requires 72 engineering hours over 12 active business days: six hours per active day, or 30 hours in a five-day delivery week. The $38,000 delivery budget values prospective work at the stated planning rate. The retained sensitivity assumes that the entire package value is paid in cash over scheduled work dates, with no entered opening balance. A rollback selects a retained release while preserving later purchases and fulfilled output. A receiving-host restore reconciles operations after the backup point before continuing unfinished work.

During funded delivery, dependency or protocol changes are assessed against the selected Stellar SDK, x402 wire format, token/account behavior and the installations that use them. Necessary compatibility corrections return to the maintained source with the affected operating example and migration instructions. The selected provider’s sponsored-fee declaration, authorization lifetime, accepted payment flow and transaction payload remain explicit parts of that compatibility review.

At handover, the maintainer receives known limitations, open support cases and the continuation procedure for each one. The installed release and usable customer output remain available for self-operation. Paid care is separately scoped around the actual hosting, response and upgrade responsibilities; the grant’s 400 hours and $38,000 fund the prospective six-package delivery described here.
